correctness.rationale: An exact characteristic-two translation identity makes the six-coordinate hypersurface the projective cone of the smooth Clebsch surface, with one multiplicity-three vertex. The smooth base has 27 geometric lines and no plane; hence the cone has exactly 27 planes. For every such plane, the two base normal-derivative binary quadrics have no common root, so they admit no linear syzygy, proving zero Fano tangent space and reducedness. The standalone exact finite-field checker enumerates all 357 lines of P3(F4) and exactly 27 contained lines, 15 Frobenius fixed and six pairs. The 27 line classes generate Picard rank 7, forcing Frobenius squared to act trivially; the 15 F2-points yield Picard eigenvalues +1 six and -1 one, establishing all-extension point counts and zeta formula without extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Kondō 2011 Section 2 and Dolgachev 2015 Section 2 give the classical ten-node, fifteen-plane Segre configuration with the same equations, but their inspected sections do not analyze its characteristic-two fiber. Vikulova 2023/2024 discusses the fifteen-fixed/six-paired Frobenius action on a smooth cubic surface, which alone does not establish the cone over this surface or the reduced 27-plane Fano scheme of a singular cubic threefold. Kadyrsizova et al. 2020 study cubic surfaces. Actual published-finding corpus searches and accessible prior research records found no coverage of the triple cone vertex plus Fano scheme; the own nearest item be1de342... assumes characteristic at least five. Historical priority remains qualified.

value.rationale: The natural mod-2 fiber of the Segre cubic changes the geometry of a distinguished cubic threefold: ten ordinary double points coalesce to a single triple cone vertex, and its finite Fano scheme of planes increases from 15 to 27 while staying reduced. The arithmetic splitting (15 rational planes, six quadratic pairs) and all-degree zeta formula identify an exceptional reduction boundary relevant to degenerations, rational planes and arithmetic geometry; not an arbitrary numerical slice or textbook reformulation.
